issues.description: StockIngredient uses different getter names for the ingredient name across template and solution. In the template, StockIngredient exposes getIngredientName(), and Stock.findStockIngredient(...) calls x.getIngredientName(). In the solution, StockIngredient exposes getName(), and Stock.findStockIngredient(...) calls x.getName(). This inconsistency can lead to compilation errors or confusion when students implement/find ingredients based on the provided starter code versus the reference behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align on a single getter name across all artifacts (prefer getName() to match the UML field name `name`). Either rename template getIngredientName() to getName() and update template Stock.findStockIngredient(...), or add a delegating getName() method in the template while keeping getIngredientName() for backward compatibility.

issues.description: The problem statement/UML are inconsistent about whether SealSaloon.stock is static. The text explicitly requires `stock` to be static (shared across all saloon instances), but the UML shows a regular association from SealSaloon to Stock without any static marker, which suggests an instance field. The solution implements `private static final Stock stock`, matching the text but not the UML depiction, potentially confusing students about the required field nature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the UML and text consistent: mark `stock` as static in the UML (e.g., underline or `{static}`) or revise the diagram/wording to clearly indicate that `stock` is shared across instances.
